Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use."}, "publicationDate": "2026-05-01", "authors": [{"authorId": "2320273371", "name": "Emre Burak Ertu\u015f"}], "abstract": "In nanomaterial research, accurate determination of particle size and morphology from Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) images is a fundamental requirement. Conventional approaches predominantly rely on explicit segmentation, which necessitates laborious manual annotation or parameter tuning, particularly when dealing with agglomerated particles or complex morphologies. In this study, we present a novel, segmentation free framework for ranking and estimating particle size ratios directly from SEM images using a similarity driven deep learning approach. Unlike traditional supervised methods that require large datasets of real annotated microscopy images, our method utilizes a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) trained exclusively on synthetically generated SEM-like images. This network learns a morphology aware embedding space where particle size information is implicitly encoded, allowing for relative size ordering and comparative assessment through embedding based retrieval. Evaluation on real SEM datasets demonstrates that the proposed framework achieves robust ranking performance and visual consistency without the need for pixel level ground truth masks. By replacing absolute metrological segmentation with a framework based on similarity-driven ranking and assisted inference, this study introduces a practical and operator\u00a0independent approach that enables rapid screening of materials."}}, {"citingPaper": {"paperId": "dd3aa363101bd1fa5531bb5d06df2e5c8a7fe4be", "externalIds": {"DOI": "10.1088/2632-2153/ae5500", "CorpusId": 286722142}, "url": "https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/dd3aa363101bd1fa5531bb5d06df2e5c8a7fe4be", "title": "Deep metric learning for explainable glaucoma diagnosis", "venue": "Machine Learning: Science and Technology", "year": 2026, "citationCount": 0, "openAccessPdf": {"url": "https://doi.org/10.1088/2632-2153/ae5500", "status": "GOLD", "license": "CCBY", "disclaimer": "Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://api.unpaywall.org/v2/10.1088/2632-2153/ae5500?email=<INSERT_YOUR_EMAIL> or https://doi.org/10.1088/2632-2153/ae5500, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. This paper focuses on the k-nearest neighbor explanation-by-example method, which consists of providing explanations for a model\u2019s predictions by referencing similar examples from the training data. We use deep metric learning (DML) to obtain a distance measure between images in order to provide an explanation for the models\u2019 predictions. A comprehensive analysis of four widely-used DML loss functions was conducted across four convolutional neural network architectures (ResNet50, VGG19, InceptionV3, and Xception) to assess both classification performance and explainability. Here we introduce RetiZero, a vision-language model that incorporates knowledge from over 400 fundus diseases. The model is pre-trained on 341,896 fundus images with accompanying text descriptions gathered from diverse sources across multiple ethnicities and countries. RetiZero demonstrates exceptional performance across various downstream tasks including zero-shot disease recognition, image-to-image retrieval, clinical diagnosis assistance, few-shot fine-tuning, and cross-domain disease identification. In zero-shot scenarios, it achieves Top-5 accuracies of 0.843 for 15 diseases and 0.756 for 52 diseases, while for image-to-image retrieval, it scores 0.950 and 0.886 respectively. Notably, RetiZero\u2019s Top-3 zero-shot performance exceeds the average diagnostic accuracy of 19 ophthalmologists from Singapore, China, and the United States. The model particularly enhances clinicians\u2019 ability to diagnose rare fundus conditions, highlighting its potential value for integration into clinical settings where diverse eye diseases are encountered. Previous ophthalmic foundation models have struggled to generalize effectively to diverse and rare fundus diseases, restricting their clinical applicability. Alhussein"}, {"authorId": "2219492209", "name": "Imran Arshad Choudhry"}, {"authorId": "31957553", "name": "Khursheed Aurangzeb"}, {"authorId": "13600677", "name": "Tariq Khan"}], "abstract": "Medical image retrieval is essential to modern medical treatment because it enables doctors to diagnose and treat a variety of illnesses. In this study, we present an innovative technique for selecting the methodology of medical images by combining textural and visual information. Knowing the imaging process behind an idea, such as a chest X-ray, skin dermatology, or breast histopathology image, may be extremely helpful to healthcare professionals since it can aid in image investigation and provide important information about the imaging technique used. We use deep learning-based feature engineering to do this, using both the textural and visual components of healthcare images. We extract detailed visual information from the images using a predefined Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). The Global-Local Pyramid Pattern (GLPP), Zernike moments, and Haralick are also used to physically separate the pertinent parts from the images\u2019 other visual and factual aspects. These essential characteristics, such as image modality and imaging technique-specific characteristics, provide additional information about the technology. We employ a feature fusion method that incorporates the depictions obtained from the two modalities in order to combine the textural and visual elements. This fusion process, which improves the discrimination capacity of the feature vectors, makes accurate modality classification possible. We conducted trials on a sizable dataset consisting of various medical images to assess the effectiveness of our proposed method. The results indicate that, in comparison to conventional methods, our technique outperforms modality retrieval, with a precision of 95.89 and a recall of 96.31. The accuracy and robustness of the classification task are greatly creased by the combination of textural and visual data. Through the integration of textural and visual information, our work offers a unique method for recovering the modality of medical images. This method has the potential to greatly improve the speed and accuracy of medical image processing and diagnosis by helping experts rapidly and accurately identify the imaging technology being utilized."}}]}
